theory.intro: A **z-score** (or **standardised score**) tells you how many standard deviations a value sits from the mean. A positive $z$ means the value is above the mean; a negative $z$ means it is below.
facts: The formula is $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$, where $x$ is the value, $\mu$ is the mean and $\sigma$ is the standard deviation.
Subtract the mean from the value, never the other way round; reversing the subtraction reverses the sign of $z$.
A value above the mean gives a positive $z$, and a value below the mean gives a negative $z$.
A value equal to the mean gives $z = 0$.
The size of $z$ is a count of standard deviations, so $z = -1.5$ is $1.5$ standard deviations below the mean.
A $z$-score has no units, so it can be compared even when the raw values are marks, seconds or grams.
Round $z$ as the question directs; otherwise give two decimal places.
steps: Substitute the value, the mean and the standard deviation

foundation.question_text: A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 80$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 6$. Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 68$.
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 35$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 8$. Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 47$.
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 11.9$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 2.5$. Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 13.4$.
What is the $z$-score of a value that lies $2.5$ standard deviations below the mean?
foundation.solution_text:
The $z$-score counts standard deviations from the mean, and below the mean is negative.
$z = -2.5$

foundation.question_text: The masses of apples in a crate have a mean of $145$ g and a standard deviation of $12$ g. Calculate the $z$-score of an apple with a mass of $154$ g.
Ella's $z$-score in a test was $-0.8$. Describe her result in terms of the mean and standard deviation of the test.
foundation.solution_text:
The $z$-score is negative, so Ella's mark was below the mean.
Her mark was $0.8$ standard deviations below the mean of the test.

development.question_text: A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 34$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 6$. Calculate the $z$-score of the value $x = 27$, correct to two decimal places.
The monthly rainfall at a weather station has a mean of $62$ mm and a standard deviation of $7.5$ mm. Calculate the $z$-score of a month with $74$ mm of rain.
Travel times on a bus route have a mean of $38$ minutes and a standard deviation of $4.5$ minutes. Calculate the $z$-score of a trip that takes $31$ minutes, correct to two decimal places.

In a test the mean was $64$ and the standard deviation was $8$. Copy and complete the table of standardised scores.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} \text{Student} & \text{Ana} & \text{Bo} & \text{Chi} & \text{Dev} \\ \hline \text{Mark} & 76 & 56 & 64 & 70 \\ \hline z\text{-score} & \ & \ & \ & \ \end{array}$
Annual rainfall in a town has a mean of $1180$ mm and a standard deviation of $145$ mm. Calculate the $z$-score of a year with $995$ mm of rain, correct to two decimal places.
Two values from the same dataset have $z$-scores of $1.2$ and $-0.4$. Which value is further from the mean, and by how many standard deviations further?
development.solution_text:
Distance from the mean is the size of the $z$-score, ignoring its sign.
The first value is $1.2$ standard deviations from the mean and the second is $0.4$ standard deviations from the mean.
$1.2 - 0.4 = 0.8$
The value with $z = 1.2$ is further from the mean, by $0.8$ standard deviations.

mastery.question_text:
The times, in seconds, taken by eight students to solve a puzzle are
$12, \ 15, \ 9, \ 14, \ 11, \ 17, \ 10, \ 16$
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation, then find the $z$-score of the slowest time. Give the standard deviation and the $z$-score correct to two decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Write the formula**
$z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$
2. **Substitute the value, the mean and the standard deviation**
From the statistics mode of the calculator,
$\mu = 13$
$\sigma = 2.7386...$
$\approx 2.74$
The slowest time is the largest, $x = 17$.
$z = \dfrac{17 - 13}{2.7386...}$
3. **Evaluate and round**
$= 1.4606...$
$\approx 1.46$

mastery.question_text: A machine fills bottles with a mean of $502$ mL and a standard deviation of $1.6$ mL. A bottle is rejected if its $z$-score is below $-2.5$ or above $2.5$. Calculate the $z$-score of a bottle containing $497$ mL and state whether it is rejected.
mastery.solution_text:
$z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$
$= \dfrac{497 - 502}{1.6}$
$= \dfrac{-5}{1.6}$
$= -3.125$
This is below $-2.5$, so the bottle is rejected.

mastery.question_text: Times for a $5$ km fun run are normally distributed with a mean of $27$ minutes $30$ seconds and a standard deviation of $2$ minutes $15$ seconds. Calculate the $z$-score of a runner who finishes in $23$ minutes.
